text:
sam: quick thought from the rollout spike: instead of a single holdout score we could use a soft-lock per-variant that prevents automatic routing changes for a short window and exposes a slow reentry path. keeps users predictable when signals bounce.

juan: soft-lock? how is that different from the holdout window we've been discussing?

sam: think of it as a state machine: UNLOCKED -> SOFT_LOCK (no auto-enable, only manual or staggered reentry) -> HARD_LOCK (full traffic cut). transitions driven by a rule engine combining error-rate/latency/quality.

emily: +1 on state machine model. easier to reason about for Console UX. can we surface states and the transition history?

sam: yes. Console should show current state, last transition reason, and a small timeline sparkline. also allow a clear/force button. audit log entry required.

zhao: operational question: where do we keep the lock state? in control-plane memory, Redis, or in the metrics tier?

juan: leaning toward ephemeral control-plane cache with fallback to metrics if node fails. reason: we want immediate decisions and low read fanout. but must have a canonical durable store for Private.

sam: agreed. propose: default for Hosted = in-memory sharded store + periodic checkpoint to durable store (compact snapshot). Private must implement storage adapter interface (Redis/Postgres backed). if adapter unavailable, degrade to metrics-evaluator-only.

claire: how do we avoid cross-tenant amplification? e.g., one noisy tenant shouldn't starve controller resources.

sam: every tenant lock is capped: TTL, fixed-size entry, LRU eviction. plus a global token-bucket for reentry ops so one tenant can't flood re-enables.

metrics-bot: p95 latency alert firing on model-m-3 for tenant:acme (current:820ms, threshold: 700ms)

emily: that alert should increment the soft-lock counter for acme. what about small tenants with low traffic where single events look catastrophic?

juan: normalize by requests-per-minute and require min_samples=5 before any lock-trigger. fallback: if below floor, mark as "manual-review" and notify customeer success.

sam: reentry strategy: when score decays below threshold we don't reenable instantly. instead we put variant into a STAGED_REENTRY queue and pop with randomized backoff and global QPS limit. each reentry attempt is a small traffic slice (1-5%) and probed for 1-2 minutes before scaling up.

zhao: sounds like we need a reentry-lease token to avoid thundering herd. good idea. how long is the lease?

sam: default 2m lease with jitter +/- 30s. lease includes owner id so Console can show who initiated reentry.

emily: telemetry: we need a per-attempt trace id so we can tie reentry probe results to decision outcome. also record sample prompts/responses for quality checks (with PII scrub).

juan: privacy note: for Dedicated/Private, sampling must obey customer data policies. adapter should tell us sampling_allowed boolean. if false, skip content sample and rely on metrics only.

claire: what about long-term refactor? can we push decision evaluation into a dedicated "policy-service" with a small API (Evaluate(tenant,variant,signals)->action). keeps router simple.

sam: yes. policy-service decouples rules and lets us iterate without touching routing path. router asks policy-service for action and follows it. policy-service can be stateless (pull EMAs) or stateful (use KV) depending on deployment.

metrics-bot: note: high-cardinality EMAs are expensive. recommend sampling or rollup topic keyed by tenant/variant to reduce cost.

juan: for spike we'll prototype: (A) policy-service stateless pulling EMAs for 5k tenants and (B) stateful policy-service using Redis for 60k tenants. measure decision latency and memory.

emily: UX owners: @emily for Console states, @claire for audit/logging schema.

claire: I'll own logging contract + storage columns for transition events. include fields: tenant_id, variant_id, from_state, to_state, reason, actor, trace_id, wall_time.

sam: dev plan: 2-week spike. deliverables: load matrix, latency p99, memory profile, prototype scripts to simulate noisy tenants, and a simple Console mock.

deploy-bot: canary soft-lock-prototype v0.2 -> staging (sha:def456) :rocket:

juan: volunteers: I'll run Redis prototype, @zhao will add lease/token logic, @sam will wire policy-service stubs.

zhao: i'll add token bucket + lease code and a small invariants test.

emily: I'll mock Console flows and make sure manual overrides are clear and auditable.

sam: perfect. i'll open the spike ticket and add acceptance criteria. if spike favors stateful, follow-up RFC for storage adapter API. if stateless wins, we'll build an optimized EMA exporter to minimize query costs.

emily: tiny UX ask: show "expected reentry ETA" when a variant is in STAGED_REENTRY so teams know when to expect traffic.

sam: noted. thanks everyone :thumbsup:
